title: Deduction of tax at source on payment of interest other than interest on securities

effectivePeriod.sunsetNotes: Transitions to Section 393(1) Table 4 Item (i) of the Income-tax Act, 2025 effective 1 April 2026.

plainTextSummary: Any person (other than an individual or HUF not liable to audit under Section 44AB in the preceding FY) responsible for paying any income by way of interest other than 'Interest on securities' to a resident payee must deduct 10% tax at source. Statutory Annual Thresholds: (a) ₹40,000 where payer is a banking company, co-operative bank, or post office (₹50,000 if payee is a resident Senior Citizen u/s 80TTB); (b) ₹5,000 for all other payers (e.g. corporate borrowers, vendor trade delayed interest, inter-corporate deposits, NBFC interest). Under Section 206AA, if payee PAN is missing or inoperative, tax is deductible at 20%. Section 194A(3) provides specific exemptions for interest paid to banks, financial corporations, and interest paid by a firm to its partners. Notice: Penal interest paid under Section 16 of the MSMED Act to Micro & Small enterprises is subject to 194A withholding if exceeding ₹5,000, and is non-deductible (statutory add-back to taxable income) under Section 23 of the MSMED Act.

keyStatutoryThresholds.msmeSection16Interaction: MSME Section 16 delayed payment penal interest is subject to Section 194A withholding if exceeding ₹5,000 in a FY, and must be permanently added back to taxable income under Section 23 of the MSMED Act.
